classification.difficultyReason: Recognise each reciprocal graph, select the correct quadrants from the sign of the constant, and substitute a convenient x-value to label one point.

content.prompt: Sketch the following, and label the coordinates of any point on the curve.

answer.short: Hyperbola in quadrants I and III; asymptotes $x=0$, $y=0$; for example, $(2,2)$.
answer.worked: At $x=2$, $y=\frac42=2$. Plot and label $(2,2)$. For positive $x$, $y>0$; for negative $x$, $y<0$. Draw branches in quadrants I and III approaching, but never touching, the axes.

spec.description: Equation-driven reciprocal branches, continuation arrowheads, labelled axes and dashed guides to (2,2). Coordinate label added to satisfy the student instruction explicitly. No grid.
spec.mathematics: y=4/x, x nonzero; point (2,2); axes are asymptotes.

answer.short: Hyperbola in quadrants II and IV; asymptotes $x=0$, $y=0$; for example, $(-1,3)$.
answer.worked: At $x=-1$, $y=-\frac3{-1}=3$. Plot and label $(-1,3)$. For negative $x$, $y>0$; for positive $x$, $y<0$. Draw branches in quadrants II and IV approaching, but never touching, the axes.

spec.description: Equation-driven reciprocal branches, continuation arrowheads, labelled axes and dashed guides to (-1,3). Coordinate label added to satisfy the student instruction explicitly. No grid.
spec.mathematics: y=-3/x, x nonzero; point (-1,3); axes are asymptotes.
